human_tolerance.notes: Roosts in trees, including leaf piles, and hunts over gardens, water and open ground at dusk and after dark; is killed by cars and tall structures.

phases.name: absent
phases.note: 'In the winter, it occurs in the southeastern United States and northeastern Mexico, with greatest concentrations in coastal areas'; Missouri bats are absent from late autumn to early spring.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: Return to the eastern United States; leaf litter and tree canopies are the main roosts.

phases.name: young
phases.note: Pups are born between May and July, average three to a litter; they learn to fly about a month after being born, after which they are weaned.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Breeding season starts in the autumn; local males sire the following summer's litter.

taxonomy.note: GBIF backbone and ITIS TSN 180016; described by Müller in 1776 as Vespertilio borealis.

external.note: gbif_usage_key from the GBIF match API; itis_tsn and wikidata from Wikidata (P815) confirmed against ITIS.

range.note: 'widely distributed in eastern North America and Bermuda ... generally occurs east of the Continental Divide, including southern Canada and northeastern Mexico'.

traits.limb_count.note: A mammal with two legs; the forelimbs are modified into the wings.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: 'Its wings are long and pointed'; the wing aspect ratio and loading indicate it flies relatively quickly and is moderately maneuverable.

traits.thermoregulation.note: 'Its entire body is densely furred, including its uropatagium' - an endotherm.

traits.flight.note: Powered flight on long pointed wings.

traits.metamorphosis.note: Born as a pup attached to the mother; no metamorphosis.

traits.nest_type.note: It roosts in trees and leaf piles and builds no nest, so None is recorded.

traits.perching.note: Hangs by its feet to roost in tree canopies and leaf litter.

traits.size_class.note: Derived from mass_kg (0.01 kg is in the Tiny band).

traits.wingspan_m.note: The article gives a forearm of about 40.6 mm but no wingspan. 0.28 m is an authored estimate for a vespertilionid of that forearm length and head-to-tail length, and is not a sourced measurement.

traits.lifespan_y.note: 'Allen Kurta argues that the lifespan for an eastern red bat is about two years, although they can probably live even longer.'

traits.diet.note: 'Eastern red bats are insectivorous, preying heavily on moths, with other insect taxa also consumed.'

traits.social.note: Hunts and roosts individually in the breeding season, though red bats form colonies in winter hibernation and in some autumn roosts; Solitary 1-1 records the summer state.

traits.activity_pattern.note: A night-flying microbat; activity is confined to darkness.

traits.defense.note: 'Eastern red bats are often attacked and killed by hawks and owls, or aggressive species like blue jays and crows' - it flees threats.

traits.wariness.note: Avoids daylight and open views, hides in leaf piles, and is quick to flee; 0.7 is a judgement.

habitat.use.note: Almost all activity is aerial insectivory at dusk and after dark with tree roosts; 85/15 is a judgement informed by EltonTraits.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Roosts in trees, including leaf piles and tree canopies, and in some caves; shelter recorded as the general tag.

habitat.resources.note: Insect prey from the diet section; leaf litter, perch and cavity tags from the roosting and predator passages.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Roosts in trees near houses and hunts over gardens, but is killed by cars, tall structures and wind turbines; numeric tolerances authored.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'In the winter, it occurs in the southeastern United States and northeastern Mexico' - a migrant in Missouri.

seasonal.phases.note: Winter in the southeastern United States, return in spring, pups born May to July, and an autumn breeding season, all from the Range and Reproduction sections.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Pups born May to July that learn to fly at about a month and are weaned then; no egg stage.

look.note: Brick or rusty red fur, frosted on females, with distinctive white shoulder patches on both sexes, short rounded ears and long pointed wings; proportions authored, and biped_winged is the closest available body plan for a bat (judgement).

behavior.note: Authored parameters for this species' own fsm-aerial-night-insectivore-v1 program: roost while the sun is between -4 and 30 degrees, hunt insects within 40 m, flee at 25 m and fly below 6 C.
